definitions.explanation: A town in southern Iwate Prefecture that was the seat of the Ōshū Fujiwara clan in the 12th century. Its Buddhist temples, among them Chūsonji with its Golden Hall, became a World Heritage Site in 2011.

{平泉|ひらいずみ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中尊寺|ちゅうそんじ}→中尊寺：32958_chuusonji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{訪|おとず}れた→訪れる：07678_otozureru⟧。
{芭蕉|ばしょう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{平泉|ひらいずみ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧「{夏草|なつくさ}や{兵|つわもの}ども⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{夢|ゆめ}→夢：01519_yume⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{跡|あと}→跡：02174_ato⟧」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{詠|よ}んだ→詠む：14186_yomu⟧。
examples.english: At Hiraizumi, Bashō wrote, "Summer grasses: all that is left of warriors' dreams."

notes:
For about a century, until it fell to ⟦{源頼朝|みなもとのよりとも}→源頼朝：31065_minamotonoyoritomo⟧ in 1189, {平泉|ひらいずみ} rivalled Kyoto as a centre of wealth and Buddhist culture in the north.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {平泉|ひらいずみ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中尊寺|ちゅうそんじ}→中尊寺：32958_chuusonji⟧: Chūsonji temple in Hiraizumi
- ⟦{中尊寺|ちゅうそんじ}→中尊寺：32958_chuusonji⟧{金色堂|こんじきどう}: the Golden Hall of Chūsonji
- {奥州藤原氏|おうしゅうふじわらし}: the Ōshū Fujiwara, the clan that ruled from Hiraizumi

CULTURAL NOTE:
Bashō visited in 1689 on the journey he wrote up in ⟦{奥|おく}の{細道|ほそみち}→奥の細道：31063_okunohosomichi⟧, and his haiku on the summer grasses there, mourning the warriors who died at Hiraizumi, is one of the best known in Japanese.
